structured_output.analysis:
There is one measured recipe so far: iso_3.15, with KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e) at avg_bits 3.148. That is right at the budget of 84617/26880, so any upgrade has to be paid for. Measured KL is above the prediction (0.436 vs 0.398), so layers interact.

The loss is concentrated in MLP layers that use 2-bit and 3-bit methods. The ledger shows cheap one-step upgrades for some of them:
- 27.up_proj: gptq_int3 0.00572 → gptq_int4 0.00217 (Ef04d8aa7bded, Efea8c18d2abc)
- 14.down_proj: rht_gptq_int2 0.00633 → rht_gptq_int3 0.00181 (E4c3f9b73e065, E90bd4b2f3645)

None of the retrieved layers is a cheap downgrade target to fund these. So:
1. Proposal 1 changes only an option that costs no bits: weight_algo.act_order=true for every GPTQ variant.
2. Proposal 2 makes the two upgrades and pays for them with a coarser group_size=256 on rht_gptq_int3.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: No change to bits. iso_3.15 measured KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e) using default GPTQ options. Most of the loss sits in GPTQ 2/3-bit MLP layers, for example 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065). These layers have heavy-tailed activations: kurtosis 1090 (E24beed188b6a) and 146 (Ef95b39c759fb). Setting weight_algo.act_order=true should cut GPTQ error on such layers.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_up2_g256
proposals.rationale:
Two upgrades:
- 27.up_proj gptq_int3→gptq_int4: single-layer KL 0.00572→0.00217 (Ef04d8aa7bded, Efea8c18d2abc).
- 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2→rht_gptq_int3: 0.00633→0.00181 (E4c3f9b73e065, E90bd4b2f3645).
Together they are predicted to save about 0.008 KL. The extra bits are paid for by halving the scale overhead of the 109 rht_gptq_int3 layers with weight.group_size=256. Base: iso_3.15, KL=0.43614 (E514ab09c524e).
